parts: 'Customer is boss' – the success and revenue of a product or service depend on customer acceptance and satisfaction. The customer service representative is the face of the business: the first impression is the last impression, so keeping customers happy and retaining them is a demanding skill.

Greet with a smile (a customer left unattended may go to another store; a welcome and smile make the customer feel valued). Offer help ('May I help you?') and inform about product qualities instead of telling the customer what to buy. Pay undivided attention: stop other work and attend to the customer first, or politely guide the customer to the right person. Be formal: converse formally and professionally; over-friendly behaviour may cause trouble. Dress professionally: neat, groomed, hair combed; a decent appearance makes customers interact confidently.

Customers can reach a business by direct contact, mobile phone, SMS, e-mail and real-time chat, so communication must be effective. Points: greet customers and verify their details (registered phone number, name); be an active listener (focus, positive body language, eye contact, nod, take notes; on the phone use phrases like 'Ok, yes I understand'); impress by repeating your understanding and seeking the customer's approval; never interrupt; use clear words and sentences (say 'Is the computer starting?' instead of 'booting'); be formal and avoid jargon and acronyms such as ASAP and FYI even in electronic communication; be courteous ('Sir/Madam, can I have the serial id?'); always appear ready to help and use positive statements instead of 'I will not be able to help you'; be cautious of words that cause unexpected reactions (say 'Kindly excuse, I am unable to hear you clearly'); check background noise and distractions; take into account the customer's preferred mode of communication (e-mail or message); seek support from colleagues and team members when stuck.

Courteous handling of an issue retains customers whereas an indifferent 'I don't know' attitude loses them and invites negative publicity; calls are recorded for quality checks; respond immediately to e-mails and calls. Follow up until the issue is resolved: schedule appointments, take feedback, transfer to a skilled technician in another department. The representative must have complete knowledge of the product and service and the latest, accurate company policies, strong communication skills, and on the phone speak slowly, stay patient and calm even if the customer is upset, listen to the complaint first and then ask small, crisp, minimum questions.
